details: Multinational Corporations (MNCs): Enterprise owning or controlling production facilities in more than one nation.

MNC Location Strategy: Research in developed nations (USA/Europe), manufacturing in low-cost countries (China), assembly & technical customer support in English-speaking nations (India). Reduces production cost by 50-60%.

Interlinking Global Production: (1) Setting up joint ventures with local domestic firms, (2) Acquiring established local companies for immediate market reach, (3) Placing sub-contracting orders with small garment/footwear producers.
evidence_or_examples: American MNC Cargill Foods acquiring Parakh Foods (Indian company with 4 oil refineries and vast distribution network), becoming India's top edible oil producer.
Ford Motors investing ₹1,700 crore near Chennai with Mahindra & Mahindra to manufacture cars for Indian and export markets.

branches.theme: 4.2 Enablers of Globalisation: Technology & Liberalisation Policy

sub_branches.concept: Transportation, IT Revolution, and 1991 Economic Reforms
details: Transportation Advances: Containerization enables fast, low-cost multi-modal freight handling across ports, railways, and trucks.
Information & Communication Technology (ICT): Internet, telecommunications, satellite communication, and digital design allow instantaneous cross-border service exports.
Trade Barriers: Quotas and import tariffs used post-independence (1950s-1980s) to protect infant domestic industries.
1991 Liberalisation Reform: Indian government removed foreign trade & investment barriers, encouraging MNC entry and market competition.
evidence_or_examples: London news magazine designed and typeset in Delhi using satellite text transmission, printed in India, and air-freighted back to London.
Container ships reducing port unloading turn-around time from days to hours while cutting freight costs.

details: World Trade Organisation (WTO): International body establishing rules for free global trade, comprising 164 member nations.
WTO Power Imbalance: Developed countries retain massive domestic agricultural subsidies while pressuring developing nations to dismantle trade barriers.

Uneven Impact in India: Benefited wealthy urban consumers (choice, quality, lower prices), large Indian MNCs (Tata Motors, Infosys, Ranbaxy expanding globally), and IT service sector. Severely hurt small manufacturers (capacitors, batteries, plastic toys shutting down) and unorganized laborers facing flexible/insecure jobs.
Fair Globalisation Policy: Government interventions needed to strictly enforce labor laws, provide credit/tech support to small units, and form developing-nation alliances at WTO.
evidence_or_examples: Ravi's capacitor manufacturing unit in Hosur forced to lay off workers and close due to duty-free capacitor imports post-1992.
Special Economic Zones (SEZs) providing 5-year tax holidays, world-class utilities, and flexible labor laws to attract MNC FDI.
